description: Exercises the builder's own web-search (Brave/SearXNG) research path. The user rules out the obvious default (USGS) and names no replacement, so the agent cannot satisfy the request from a remembered endpoint — it has to search for candidate sources, then read the docs of whichever it picks. The exclusion is load-bearing: an earlier draft without it passed by fetching the USGS docs URL straight from memory, never searching at all. Build-only on purpose: what's under test is whether research happened and shaped the build, not whether the run executes. Requires INSTANCE_AI_BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY (or N8N_INSTANCE_AI_SEARXNG_URL) on the target instance — without a provider the web-search action returns zero results and the non-empty-results expectation reds for environment reasons, not agent behaviour.

conversation.text: Every weekday morning around 8am I want a Slack message in #quake-watch listing any earthquake of magnitude 5 or above from the last 24 hours near Japan. We've had reliability trouble with the USGS feed so I'd rather not depend on it — find a different source that's free and works without an API key, and check its current docs for the request it expects.

processExpectations: The agent researched the data source with its research tool (web search, optionally followed by fetching a docs page) before writing the HTTP request — the user named no provider and asked it to find one, so picking an endpoint straight from memory without looking anything up does not satisfy this.

The web-search call returned a non-empty set of real results that the agent went on to use. An empty result set — which is what an unconfigured search provider returns — does not satisfy this, even though the agent may still finish the build from other sources.
The agent did not ask the user which API to use, what the endpoint is, or what the query parameters are — the user already said they don't know and asked the agent to find out.
The agent named the source it settled on and said it is free and usable without an API key, rather than leaving the choice unexplained.
outcomeExpectations: A Schedule Trigger fires the workflow on a recurring weekday-morning cadence.
An HTTP Request node queries a public earthquake feed that needs no API key or credential, and it is not the USGS feed the user ruled out.
The request constrains results to roughly the last 24 hours using a value computed at run time (an expression over the current date), not a hardcoded past date.
The request or a downstream filter restricts results to magnitude 5 and above and to the Japan region, rather than passing every worldwide quake through.
Quake details are read out of the response's actual nested shape (the per-event records and their magnitude/location/time fields), not from invented top-level field names.
One Slack message summarizing the matching quakes is posted to the #quake-watch channel the user named.
The workflow handles the no-quakes case without posting a misleading empty alert — either a conditional gate before the Slack step or a message that states nothing was found.
